emitter.name: Emitter
emitter.desc: Particle count, lifetime and ID encoding

shape_image_contour.name: Shape (Image Contour)
shape_image_contour.desc: Upload an image → trace its outline (by brightness, alpha or an RGB channel) → turn it into a formula with Elliptic Fourier Descriptors. Outputs x/y/z — lays particles out in the shape of a logo, text or silhouette

noise3d.name: Noise 3D
noise3d.desc: Choose Perlin, Simplex, Voronoi or FBM. Takes x/y/z and outputs a noise value n. It works out where it is connected automatically (on offset it is computed once; on tint/size it is recomputed for every particle). The node shows the pattern as a black-and-white image

curlnoise.name: Curl Noise
curlnoise.desc: Divergence-free (incompressible) noise vector field — outputs a force fx/fy/fz. Use it for fluid-like swirling motion such as smoke, fire and eddies. The flow option makes the pattern drift over time. The preview shows the field as arrows

vecfield_image.name: Vector Field (Image)
vecfield_image.desc: A custom vector field baked onto a grid from an uploaded image — outputs a force fx/fy. Three modes: brightness gradient, mask edge, or RGB flow map. Use it to make particles flow along a logo, pattern or custom shape

curlturb.name: Turbulence (Curl FBM)
curlturb.desc: Curl Noise stacked over several octaves for multi-scale turbulence — outputs a force fx/fy/fz. Same idea as Houdini POP Turbulence and Unity VFX Graph "Turbulence". Small details ride on top of big swirls, giving complex smoke- or cloud-like motion. The flow option makes it drift over time

vortexfield.name: Vortex Field
vortexfield.desc: Swirling flow around an axis (viscous coupling + centripetal pull) — outputs fx/fy/fz. Same idea as Unity VFX Graph "Vortex" and Unreal Niagara "Vortex Velocity Force". For typhoons, tornadoes and particles being sucked into a whirl. The pulse option makes the strength throb periodically

attractorfield.name: Attractor / Point Force
attractorfield.desc: Pulls particles toward a point (+) or pushes them away (−) — outputs fx/fy/fz. Same as Unity "Sphere Attraction" and Niagara "Point Attraction Force". For implosions, collect effects and magnets. The pulse option makes the strength beat like a heart

directionalfield.name: Directional Force
directionalfield.desc: A constant push in one direction (gravity or wind) — outputs fx/fy/fz. Same as Niagara "Gravity Force" / "Wind Force". The basic force for falling or wind-blown effects. The gust option varies the strength over time

windzone.name: Wind Zone
windzone.desc: Local wind that blows only inside a box or sphere — outputs fx/fy/fz. Same as Unity "Wind Zone" and Niagara's volume-limited Wind Force. Use it for wind in one area only (a draft through a window, a local gust). The gust option varies the strength; together with turbulence both direction and strength waver naturally

wall.name: Wall · collision
wall.desc: Keeps particles inside box walls (min/max) and bounces them off — input x/y/z → output x/y/z. Set friction and bounce per wall (bouncy like a slime block); the eye icon shows the walls in the 3D preview. Place it between a position output (Shape, Noise…) and the Output offset.

dragfield.name: Drag / Damping
dragfield.desc: Outputs a drag coefficient (based on Bedrock's linear_drag_coefficient; same idea as Niagara "Drag Force"). Note: Output has no drag socket — this editor moves particles by formula, not by the engine's physics — so the value only works as a plain number you feed into other nodes (for example a Formula)

buoyancyfield.name: Buoyancy
buoyancyfield.desc: Buoyancy from a temperature difference (T − T_ambient) — outputs fx/fy/fz. Same idea as Houdini POP Buoyancy. Makes hot smoke or fire rise. If temperature is not connected it cools down automatically over emitter_age (time since the emitter started) or particle_age (each particle's own age)

math.name: Formula
math.desc: Write any formula; it is converted to Molang for you. Has a t (time) input — connect it to another node's strength or radius (Vortex, Attractor…) to animate it over time

constant.name: Constant
constant.desc: Outputs a single fixed value — a value node for Accumulate's in (increase per second) or init (start value), Formula inputs and so on

remap.name: Remap
remap.desc: Maps a value from the range [inMin, inMax] to [outMin, outMax] (optional clamp) — same as the Remap/Fit node in Unity and Houdini. An easy way to bring noise or field strength into the range you want

dissipationfield.name: Dissipation
dissipationfield.desc: Exponential fade based on a half-life → outputs out. Models smoke density, heat or alpha thinning out over time (D_t+1 = D_t·(1 − α·Δt)). Connect it to tint.a or size for smoke and embers that fade naturally. The automatic time axis can be emitter_age (time since the emitter started) or particle_age (each particle's own age)

accumulate.name: Accumulate
accumulate.desc: Adds up a value over time without storing state (recomputed every frame from the particle id and time) — out = init + ∫ in dt. Use it for "how much has built up so far", such as spin angle or distance travelled. Supports clamp, wrap and reset

gradient.name: Color Gradient
gradient.desc: Blends several color stops along t (0–1) → outputs r/g/b. Edit it on a real gradient bar (same idea as the Gradient node in Unity and Houdini)

curve.name: Curve (Over-Life)
curve.desc: A curve over the particle's life (0–1) → connect it to size, alpha and so on. Draw the curve directly on the graph (tap to add points, drag to move them)

flipbook.name: Flipbook UV
flipbook.desc: Plays a texture atlas (a grid of frames) in order over time — outputs u/v/uv_size.w/uv_size.h. Same as Unity "Texture Sheet Animation" and Niagara "Sub UV". Connect it straight to the Output uv sockets for sprite-sheet animation (explosions, sparks, smoke frames)

threshold.name: Threshold / Dissolve
threshold.desc: Compares a value with a threshold and outputs 0 or 1 (softness smooths the edge) — same as "Step" in Shader Graph. Feed it Noise 3D and animate the threshold with a Curve for a dissolve effect that follows the noise pattern. Connect the output to tint.a

sub_emitter.name: Sub Emitter
sub_emitter.desc: Same as Emitter plus a bone input. A separate particle effect that is fired by an Event

event.name: Event
event.desc: Fire condition (creation / expiration / timeline) + which values to copy → triggers a Sub Emitter

particle_event.name: Particle Event
particle_event.desc: Fires on each particle's creation, expiration or timeline → Sub Emitter, sound or Molang (particle_lifetime_events)
